COMPARATIVE FRAMEWORKS FOR 3D URBAN PATH PLANNING | CAPSTONE PRESENTATION
Problem: On a 3D cell graph, find minimum 3D path length from start to goal while staying at or above the buffer altitude field B.
Edge cost: Euclidean 3D distance between neighboring states (26-connectivity by default); all costs ≥ 0.
Method: Best-first search — always expand the node with smallest f = g + h (min-heap); g = cost from start, h = straight-line 3D distance to goal.
Guarantee: Optimal on this discretized graph when h is admissible (underestimates true cost); straight-line 3D h satisfies this.
OD only where H = 0; start/goal at B; on ground NFZ floor → vertical-only moves (like Dijkstra lift); no horizontal travel at clearance floor
